summary: SCIM displayName with emoji base64-encoding mangles SAML attribute, blocking service-account scheduled jobs
description:
Issue summary: Customer's SCIM provisioning creates service accounts whose displayName contains emoji (e.g., 'ExportJob❤️') and long text. The IdP appears to base64-encode the displayName when emitting the SAML assertion (attribute urn:custom:displayName). The customer's private deployment identity-proxy strips trailing '=' padding on attribute values during header normalization, which corrupts the base64 blob. This results in the RBAC role-mapper failing to parse the attribute and no tenant-scoped roles being granted to the service account.

Impact: Scheduled export workers (service accounts) provisioned via SCIM cannot assume tenant-scoped roles and receive 403 on the scheduled job endpoints. The customer reports ~100 failed jobs over the last 24 hours; business impact is delayed nightly exports.

Environment: Private deployment (customer-managed VPC), prod-us-east region. SCIM provisioning originates from Okta (SCIM connector v2). Identity-proxy version: v1.8.3 (private bundle). RBAC service version: 2.1.0.

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Provision a service account via SCIM with a long displayName containing emoji (example: 'nightly-export-batch-2026-03-09-🚀').
2) Observe SCIM create event in Okta; Okta sends to Redwood SCIM endpoint.
3) Confirm user/service account exists in Redwood console.
4) Trigger scheduled job that uses the service account credentials (or run token exchange).
5) Job fails with 403 and logs show RBAC mapping did not find tenant binding.

Observed logs/symptoms:
- On the IdP side, SAML assertion contains attribute urn:custom:displayName with value looking like base64 (example: 'bm...Zy0yMDI2LTAzL...==').
- Identity-proxy access logs show header X-Raw-Assertion: 'urn:custom:displayName=bm...Zy0yMDI6LT0' (note trailing '==' changed to '=0' after header normalization).
- RBAC service logs: "role-mapper: attribute decode failed: invalid padding" and subsequently "no-tenant-binding for principal service-account:nightly-export-2026".
- Customer console shows service account present but lacking tenant bindings.

Requested from customer: SCIM payload (redacted), a sample SAML assertion (base64), and a HAR/wire capture of the assertion flow.

investigation_notes:
Hypothesis: Okta SCIM/displayName is being base64-encoded by the IdP because it contains non-ASCII (emoji) characters. The SAML path then emits the base64 string as an attribute value. Our identity-proxy has a legacy header normalization step which assumed header values would be UTF-8 strings and, when encountering characters outside an allowed set or when length > 120, performs URL-decoding and trims padding '=' characters (bug introduced in v1.7.9). Trimming '=' corrupts base64 payloads and causes downstream role-mapper to fail base64 decode, so the attribute used for role resolution becomes invalid.

Evidence collected:
- Decoded SAML assert: urn:custom:displayName = 'bm...==', decoded -> 'nightly-export-2026-03-09-🚀'.
- Identity-proxy sanitized header: padding replaced/mangled, visible in canary logs: 'bm...=0'.
- Role-mapper error trace: 'base64: invalid padding at offset 248'.
- Reproduced locally by sending a synthetic SAML assertion with base64-encoded displayName and passing through identity-proxy v1.8.3; observed same mangling.

Temporary mitigation tested: disable header padding trim in identity-proxy and restart subset; immediate repro job succeeded when routed through updated proxy.

Open questions:
- Whether other attributes may be affected (e.g., urn:custom:jobLabel) — quick scan shows a few other attributes with non-ascii may be base64-encoded by IdP.
- Whether SCIM configuration at customer side can be adjusted to avoid IdP base64-encoding (customer prefers not to remove emoji).

Next steps and owners:
- SRE/Platform (Marco): propose a hotfix to identity-proxy to preserve header raw values and only perform normalization for known safe attributes. Draft PR created. (see related_github_prs).
- Support (Aisha): coordinate with customer on re-provisioning plan and bulk remediation for existing affected service accounts.
resolution:
Mitigation applied: We deployed a canary config change to the customer's identity-proxy (disabled header padding trim) which restored correct attribute delivery for test jobs. Customer confirmed a single repro job succeeded.

Permanent fix plan: merge PR to identity-proxy to avoid trimming '=' from header values and add unit tests for base64-like attributes. Add detection/alerting when attributes look like base64 but decode to non-ASCII characters and document recommended SCIM mapping.

Workarounds for customer until fix is fully rolled out:
- Re-provision affected service accounts (fast but may be disruptive).
- Update SCIM template to populate a separate ASCII-only attribute (e.g., serviceName) without emoji and map RBAC to that attribute.

Follow-ups:
- Patch release scheduled for 2026-03-15 to identity-proxy v1.8.4 with hotfix and tests.
- Support to run a bulk remediation script (optionally) to repair attribute values for already affected service accounts; script to be delivered after customer signs off.

Status: Waiting on Customer to sign off on patch rollout plan and choose remediation approach.
